column1: # Runtime witness enumeration for the X11 final-vocabulary ADR (second independent witness)
# Method: observe the PRODUCT'S OWN OUTPUT by running bin/qmx against various targets, never by
# reading source code that declares rule/channel/metric names, and never by reading any
# already-prepared enumeration (per the task brief: enumeration-*.tsv and
# The one deliberate exception: a single `grep -rn "'annotation.directive'"  src/` was run to
# confirm that "annotation.directive" is an internal producer-rule-name that is never itself
# published as a finding channel (its four concrete children are). This is noted inline below.
# All commands were run from the repository root, on branch
# claude/x11-final-vocabulary, with `php bin/qmx` (project dev checkout, not a phar).
#     -> gives the 51 RULE names (not channel names) and their --rule-opt keys; used only to
#        know which --rule-opt overrides exist, and as a cross-check that every rule name maps
#        to at least one observed channel (some rules publish several distinct child channels;
#        one rule, annotation.directive, publishes none of its own name — see below).
#     -> whole-directory sweeps: the project's own source tree (default and strict presets),
#        the finding-gate/ directory (which physically contains ~68 PHP fixture and tooling
#        files used by the finding-equivalence gate, scanned with the ROOT qmx.yaml), and the
#        tests/ tree (PHPUnit tests plus tests/Fixtures/*, also under the ROOT qmx.yaml).
#   For each subdirectory of finding-gate/cases/ that carries its own qmx.yaml, run that case
#   with its own config (this is how the finding-equivalence gate itself exercises each
#   fixture family — a case's fixtures are calibrated against its own thresholds, not the
#   (cases: annotations, applied-threshold, complexity, coupling, cycle, design, disabled-rule,
#    disabled-rule-duplication, duplication, excluded-path, health, layers, only-rules,
#   Three targeted --rule-opt overrides were used to raise coverage for channels whose default
#   thresholds are not tripped anywhere in reach (still "observe the runtime output", per the
#   task brief's explicit invitation to combine options to raise coverage; never inferred from
#   source, only confirmed by the finding actually appearing in a subsequent run):
#   Cross-format spot-check (no new channel ids found beyond what --format=json already showed;
#   both formats republish the same "channel"/"check_name" string):
#   --format=metrics emits one JSON object per analysed symbol (type: file, class, method,
#   function, namespace, project), each carrying a "metrics" map of key -> value. All 296
#   observed keys below were pooled across these seven runs and across every symbol type.
#   name         the exact string observed in the product's own output
#   observed_in  comma-separated run labels (see command list above) where this name was
#                actually seen — not where it was merely expected
#   notes        free text: how a hard-to-reach name was actually triggered, or what is
#                project-specific/open-ended about it. Empty for the common case.
#   59 unique channel names observed (from `violations[].channel` across every run above)
#   296 unique metric-key names observed (from `symbols[].metrics` keys across every run above)
# ---- WHAT THIS METHOD DOES NOT SEE ----
#   1. Rule names vs published channels are NOT the same vocabulary. `bin/qmx rules` lists 51
#      rule names; only 44 of those ever appear verbatim as a runtime channel. Confirmed
#        - annotation.directive: never published itself. Its four concrete children
#          appear in output. A single `grep` on the producer-rule-name constant in
#          confirmed this is structural, not a coverage gap of this run.
#        - computed: a generic label for user-defined computed metrics. Only one concrete
#          instance is reachable from this repository's own trees: computed.branch-load,
#          declared solely in finding-gate/cases/health/qmx.yaml. The set of possible
#          "computed.*" channel names is open-ended (whatever a user's qmx.yaml formula section
#          names) and cannot be enumerated from product output alone.
#      Conversely, four channels exist that have NO matching entry in `bin/qmx rules` at all —
#      they are sibling diagnostics of architecture.layer-violation, not separately listed rules:
#      architecture.potential-shadow, plus architecture.pending-layer-matched. These were only
#      observed via finding-gate/cases/layers/ (its own qmx.yaml deliberately misconfigures the
#      layer policy to trip each one).
#   2. Channels that needed a threshold override to appear at all — meaning their DEFAULT
#      configuration in this repository's own qmx.yaml (or the absence of any config) does not
#      surface them anywhere in src/, tests/, or finding-gate/, only after deliberately
#        - design.noc (default warning/error=10; no fixture in reach has more than 3 direct
#        - maintainability.index (default warning/error=35; no file in src/ or tests/ scores
#          that low; forced to warning=100 against src/)
#        - architecture.unassigned-class (silent unless --rule-opt mode=... is set; forced to
#          mode=error against tests/Fixtures, which the src/-shaped layer patterns do not cover)
#      A different corpus, a different --rule-opt value, or a future codebase that regresses
#      past these thresholds could all surface the same channel through the normal default path
#      — this run only proves the channel EXISTS and what it looks like, not that it fires
#      under any specific project's real-world configuration.
#   3. architecture.layer-violation is enabled at severity=error in the project's own root
#      qmx.yaml, yet src/ itself reports zero findings on this channel in every src/ run — the
#      codebase is currently self-compliant with its own layer policy. It was only observed via
#      the finding-gate/cases/layers/ fixture, which deliberately plants a violation. A
#      self-compliant tree is legitimately invisible to this method for this specific channel;
#      absence in src/ is not evidence the channel is unused in practice.
#   4. Rules/channels that fire only under conditions this run never constructed:
#          sql-injection, xss) never appear in src/ or tests/ output — only in
#          finding-gate/cases/security/ and the finding-gate/ pooled run, both purpose-built
#          fixtures. Confirms these rules exist and their five channel names, but says nothing
#          about how often they'd fire on arbitrary real-world PHP.
#          absent from src/ (the project's own code is clean on these smells by construction),
#          only observed via finding-gate/ and finding-gate/cases/smells/.
#        - architecture.circular-dependency: absent from src/ and finding-gate/ pooled run,
#          only via finding-gate/cases/cycle/ and tests/ fixtures.
#   5. Metric-key COVERAGE per symbol type was pooled across seven runs, but no run guarantees
#      every declared metric appears at every symbol type it is theoretically defined for — a
#      metric absent from all seven pooled runs simply never appeared in a "symbols[].metrics"
#      map, and could still exist under a symbol type or project configuration this run never
#      constructed (e.g. a metric gated behind a disabled-by-default collector, or one that only
#      populates under global/cross-file context this run's targets never exercised).
#   6. --format=health and the JSON "health" summary block, and --format=text/summary, were not
#      separately mined for additional names: a spot check on src/ (--format=sarif and
#      --format=gitlab) showed both simply republish the same "channel"/"check_name" strings
#      already captured from --format=json, so no further formats were pursued for channels.
#      --format=summary/text/checkstyle/github/suppressed/html were not run at all; they were
#      judged unlikely to add find-able names beyond channel/metric-key given the sarif/gitlab
#      spot check, but that judgment was not independently verified for each format.
#   7. --preset=legacy and --preset=ci were not run (only default and --preset=strict); they
#      change thresholds, not the vocabulary of possible names, so they were judged unlikely to
#      add new channels beyond what --preset=strict and the forced --rule-opt runs already
#      surfaced — but this was not empirically verified.
